segments: This was at the meeting in Washington, D.C.
with President Eisenhower, and Nixon was in
on the meeting, and I told President Eisenhower
at the time when we showed the various shots
that we had that this looked like a German
Honda View 2, and he said, I think you're
right.
At that point, when he said, I think you're
right, did he elaborate on this whole issue
of what was German and what was not in terms
of the disks?
No, he didn't. He just agreed with me that
that looked like a Honda View 2, and he said
yes, it was. So he had to be familiar with
the different types of crafts, just from
looking
at pictures, you know. I always had the
feeling that Eisenhower knew more than we
knew, and
that he knew a lot more than what Nixon knew.
Nixon wasn't completely in the loop on this
thing, because Nixon was always frustrated
that he was on the outside looking in.
And what time of day did you travel, and
what was the process?
Yeah, same way. We flew up to Washington, D.C.,
to see the airport. The limo picked us up,
took us to a hotel, stayed overnight. We
were told to go to the Capitol building, and
that
we'd have a meeting in the Capitol building
with Eisenhower and Nixon and some other CIA
officials
from Langland. So we waited in this rotunda,
and pretty soon a guard come up to us, and
he says,
I've gotten a call that they had called and
changed the location. And we had the meeting
with Nixon and Eisenhower at a meeting room
in the FBI building. In that last meeting,
we had a few
FBI officials that came to the meeting that
were involved with the project. No Air Force.
They'd already
talked to the Air Force and all the other
forces the week before. So we had to get
back in the limo and go over
there. Near the White House? Not too far
away, no. So you drove from the Capitol?
To the FBI headquarters, and they ushered us
into the meeting room. It was about the
third or fourth
floor. We went in, and Eisenhower and Nixon
were already there. So he got our
information.
How many people, and where is Nixon, and
where is Eisenhower? When we came in, the
room was well lit. It was like a
conference room in the FBI headquarters
building, and Eisenhower was there, and
Nixon was there, both sitting
down already at the table. They were
discussing some type of paperwork, and the
FBI people came in right behind us,
three of them. Was J. Edgar Hoover with it?
No. No, he was not there.
Eisenhower. Nixon are sitting there talking
about paperwork. What happened?
Eisenhower, he asked the FBI people, do you
have much material? They said that they had
a reasonably good
stack to go over, and they asked us what we
had, and we said that we really didn't have
much. At that time,
we probably had ten or a dozen cases to
cover, and he said, "We're taking you first.
Come forward and
show us what you have." So we brought the
suitcase up.
Ms. Anthony and you, only from the CIA? Yes,
and we opened it up, laid it down on the
floor,
and took out the big folder we had
everything in it, and then laid out all the
photographs. And that's
when the first photograph I showed him was
the Argentine one, and I said, "This looks
like a
hominibu to German craft," and Eisenhower
said, "I think you're right." And that's
when Nixon looked at
Eisenhower, looked at me, and just sort of
looked totally stunned. So I have a feeling
that Eisenhower
kept Nixon out of the loop. When I mentioned
the German craft, Eisenhower did not
question it,
so he already had known about the German
space program who knows how long before.
Ms. Did Anthony say anything?
Mr. Anthony said, "Yes, I agree. This
resembles the German crafts from Argentina."
Ms. And Eisenhower doesn't pick up on this
and talk about, "Do we know anything more?"
Mr. The only thing he said was, "We have
chips down in the area that the CIA had any
knowledge about
how many of these crafts are being reported
coming out of Argentina." And then we gave
them that report
that we had gotten that our naval vessels
had radar screen contacts of saucers coming
in from outer space
and going into around the crest to the south
polar regions and also coming in and down
into the Argentine
area. Ms. This is Eisenhower saying this?
Mr. That was part of a report that we had
and that we had radar contacts.
Ms. When you said that?
Mr. Eisenhower says, "That is to be expected.
We expected this." It's something he was
already familiar with.
He may have gotten a report from CIA
headquarters on something like that when it
first came out.
Ms. Or from the National Security Council,
from the Majestic 12 people.
Mr. Yeah. Everything that came that was
reported always mentioned Majestic 12.
Ms. Did Eisenhower ever reference Majestic
Mr. Yes. At one time, we were looking at the
different photographs and he mentioned,
he had told Nixon, "This looks familiar. It
was an aerial shot over the Netherlands." He
said,
"Contact Majestic" on this. He said, "Verify
if this is the very same thing that they had
sent three months ago."
Ms. And did Nixon respond?
Mr. Yeah, he said, "Okay, I'll do this."
Ms. Did anybody ever explain why Majestic?
Why the term Majestic?
Mr. We knew it was a term for the original
people that were digging into the flying
saucer episodes.
Ms. It sounds like there were parallel
tracks of intelligence and that Majestic
would have been
working through the NSC. The CIA would have
been doing its intelligence, the FBI doing
its intelligence,
the Army, the Air Force, the Navy, and that
all these parallel tracks and sometimes
investigating each other.
And I know the Navy has tried to get into
CIA files. I've talked with a man who said
how hard they tried and how they were
blocked.
Ms. Did Eisenhower in that meeting say
anything about an understanding about
whether or not he was perceiving
that there was ally or threat or any
interpretation?
Mr. No. In fact, Nixon said that Eisenhower
had just told him that we're not gaining
enough ground
on this thing, that we need new blood,
especially the Air Force.
Ms. Did Eisenhower in this meeting in the
spring of 1959, is that when he said that he
didn't understand
why no one was getting to the bottom?
Mr. That was a quote I had mentioned earlier
that it was Nixon that said Ike is really
disappointed in this
thing and that he said that we need new
blood involved in this thing to try to move
it along because we're
not really accomplishing that much. And he
said that was Ike's word. And then when we
walked out,
the Air Force colonel had said to us, "Boy,
it looks like I'm out of a job."
Ms. Is Eisenhower saying anything with impatience,
with anger, with anything that would give
insight
that he had any sense of whether there was
hostility, any interpretation given at that
meeting about
these crafts and these beings?
Mr. The only thing he asked us, he says, "Do
you have any pictures with aliens?"
Mr. Similar to what you had before and
everything, and we told him no, that we did
not have anything with aliens.
I think we sat there about 15 minutes with
him. He looked at all of them and we told
him that all
the interviews that we had overseas with
people that had taken the pictures. We had
this one picture we
showed him that was from Holland where this
thing hovered over this little town area.
Ms. Triangle.
Mr. No, that was the round one. And that
eventually went and started going up and
then just darted and shot away at high speed.
But he mentioned alien saucer.
Ms. There has been a story that has floated
for years that Eisenhower went to see one of
the live beings in California,
and that it was covered on his daily travel
schedule as going to a dentist, but that he
actually went to see a being somewhere in
China Lake.
Mr. I never saw anything like that, any
material like that or any word during the
meeting we had.
Nothing like that was ever brought up that
he had seen an alien or spoke with an alien,
whatever he might have done.
Mr. Did Nixon say anything specifically at
that meeting in April?
Mr. No, very, very little. He said, "In your
FBI report, is there anything unusual in
that that would be interesting to
CIA as far as looking for unusual type of
crafts overseas?" And then they told us that
they had a lot of
sightings. They said, "We have some abductions.
We have..."
Mr. They said that? The FBI?
Mr. Yes.
Mr. They said they had...
Mr. We were investigating two abductions
that people claimed that they were up in the
saucer and came
back. They had a neighbor that had taken a
picture of the craft, and this one woman was
abducted.
So it tied together with two people. They
said it's probably accurate.
Mr. Then they said, "But outside of that, we
have some more cattle mutilations."
Mr. Did Eisenhower ask any questions about
mutilations and abductions?
Mr. No. So he's very familiar with that,
apparently.
Mr. Nixon or the President didn't seem like
surprised.
Mr. The question is, what did they know
about who, what, why?
Mr. I had a feeling that Eisenhower knew a
lot more, and that
Mr. Nixon kind of knew the basics, but not
in detail.
Mr. And you guys were treated only as a need
to know.
Mr. Yes.
Mr. And the President said, "If it's foreign,"
he said, "and something is hot," he says, "Call
Richard,"
because he's handling anything on the
foreign affairs bit. He said, "He's my right-hand
man on foreign affairs."
Mr. Did you, or Angie, when you got back to
Fort, were you able to find out information
about what the FBI's
abduction cases were about?
Mr. We had a few, and we asked the CIA
headquarters to give us a rundown on that
particular case
that was brought out in this meeting, but we
never got it back.
Mr. In terms of any of the discussion with
Nixon or anybody else in Washington about abductions,
do you remember anybody making the comment
of any interpretation or anything about what
the abductions could mean?
Mr. Well, we had gotten paperwork earlier
about an abduction, and the people,
the ones that were abducted were a bright
light came in their bedroom, and they floated
out the windows
and up into this craft, and then they were
operated on or had like a physical, and they
woke up in the
morning and they were back in their beds.
Mr. Well, we had gotten paperwork earlier
about an abduction, and the people, the ones
that were abducted,
